papers.title: A Fully Distributed Market Clearing Framework for Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading in Heterogeneous Virtual Power Plants
papers.authors: W He, Y Yang, Z Yang, YC Tian, Y Mishra - IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid, 2026
papers.abstract: Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) are proposed to aggregate numerous small-scale prosumers to handle their barriers in participating in Peer-to-Peer (P2P) markets due to capacity requirements. However, market clearing in P2P energy markets with multiple VPPs is challenging because of VPP heterogeneity, communication resource constraints, and the coupling between intra-and inter-VPP markets. papers.title: A Note on the Second-Order Convergence of Proximal ADMM for Non-Convex Optimization
papers.authors: J Gao, X Geng - Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications, 2026
papers.abstract: The proximal alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is an efficient algorithm for solving the linearly constrained optimization problem. This work studies the second-order convergence for proximal ADMM. By analyzing the Jacobian matrix associated with the proximal ADMM mapping, we show that the proximal ADMM avoids strict saddle points for almost all initial points. papers.title: Single-agent and multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms Ph. D. Thesis
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning is a vastly researched field nowadays. As computers continue to be even more potent, many fields that were previously handled by classical control algorithms can be solved by it. These include robotics, drone control and self-driving tasks, and even other fields such as large language model fine-tuning. papers.title: Convex Geometry in Projection Methods and the Cone of Sums of Nonnegative Circuit Polynomials
papers.abstract: Convex geometry studies convex sets and their structural and analytical properties, mainly in Euclidean spaces. Convex sets arise naturally in optimization, convex analysis, and PDEs. In this thesis, we study projection methods and the cone of sums of nonnegative circuit (SONC) polynomials. Projection methods form an efficient class of algorithms for solving feasibility problems in convex optimization, while the SONC cone is gaining importance in polynomial optimization.
